newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S., Mexico agree breakthroughs for farm trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Mexico agree breakthroughs for farm trade.

text.p: Mexico and United States on Tuesday agreed and signed several breakthroughs to boost farm trade between the two nations, the White House Press Office said in a statement.

The press office said that binational agricultural delegations meeting in Mexico for the state visit of U.S. President Bill Clinton had agreed to allow citrus fruits from Florida and Arizona states to have access to Mexican markets.
Also, it was agreed that Mexico will improve the inspection of livestock, corn, wheat and sorghum imports from the United States to accommodate expanding trade.

The White House Press Office also said the United States was to recognise that Mexico's Mexicali valley in Baja California state is free of the karnal bunt wheat disease, allowing wheat imports from that growing zone.
Also, it added that the United States will recognise Sonora state as a low risk area for hog cholera and thereby allow imports of fresh and frozen pork from Sonora to U.S. markets.
On the citrus accord, it said Mexico had restricted the importation of Florida citrus because of concerns regarding canker.

"However, a new regulatory program in Florida will control and eradicate canker. Mexico's acceptance of this regulatory approach, coupled with the citrus industry's efforts to control and eradicate the disease, could enable Florida citrus exports to Mexico to reach $2 million per year in the near term," the White House said.

On Mexico improving the inspection of livestock and crop imports, it said an agreement had been reached for Mexico to make inspectors available on an "as needed" basis at Mexican ports of entry for greens and livestock to facilitate the movement of these products.
In 1996, the White House said, 2.2 million tonnes of corn, 1.1 tonnes of sorghum and 550,000 tonnes of wheat were moved by rail through the Laredo, Texas, customs district.
"More generally, Mexican imports of corn, sorghum and wheat are projected to reach 7 million tonnes for the 1996-1997 agricultural year," the White House Press Office added.
On the karnal bunt question, it said that the U.S. Department of Agriculture and the Animal and Plant Inspection Service have concluded that Mexicali valley is a pest-free area.

"In addition, as a result of a recent binational technical inspection of the Mexicali valley and contiguous production areas, amended wheat import regulations will allow Mexican wheat imports from the Mexicali valley," it said.

On the hog cholera question in Sonora state in northern Mexico, it said the Department of Agriculture announced publication of a final ruling that specifically designates Sonora, Mexico, as a "low risk area for hog cholera".
"Such designation will allow for imports of fresh and frozen pork from this region. Already, this region ships substantial pork products to Asia and the Far East," it added.
